**Works with ReForgeDB as well as ForgeDB.** No database changes. Install over 2.2.1 and nothing in your bot needs to change.

### Added
- ReForgeDB support. Giveaways are stored with whichever of ReForgeDB and ForgeDB your bot loaded. If both are loaded, ReForgeDB is used and a warning asks you to keep only one, since both add the same functions. Before, the extension refused to start with ReForgeDB.
- `logLevel` option (`silent`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`) and the `REFORGEGIVEAWAYS_LOG_LEVEL` environment variable, like ReForgeDB and ReForgeTopGG. `debug` shows the database in use, every giveaway action (start, end, reroll, pause, resume, cancel, entries) and every entry write with its time. `trace` also shows timers and message refreshes. Every line still starts with `[ReForgeGiveaways]`.
- With ForgeDB alone, a one-time reminder at start-up to consider switching to ReForgeDB (your data is used as it is), with a link to the switching guide. It is shown once per process, shared with the other ReForge extensions, and `logLevel: "warn"` hides it.
- New exports: `ReForgeGiveawaysLogger`, `TransformEvents`, `resolveDatabaseManager`, `loadedDatabaseExtensions`, `DATABASE_EXTENSIONS` and `remindToSwitch`.

### Changed
- ReForgeGiveaways no longer imports a database package. It uses the database extension your bot loaded, with that extension's connection settings and its own `giveaways.db`.
- `@tryforge/reforge.db` and `@tryforge/forge.db` are optional peer dependencies. Before, npm installed the original ForgeDB into every bot, even bots using ReForgeDB.
- The database extension can come before or after ReForgeGiveaways in `extensions`.
- With neither database extension loaded, the bot refuses to start with a message naming both.
- `GiveawaysDatabaseManager` is deprecated and no longer used. It is kept so existing imports still work.

### Tests and CI
- The suite runs on ReForgeDB and ForgeDB. CI covers both on SQLite and PostgreSQL, on Node.js 22 and 24, plus a job on ForgeScript 2.5.0, the oldest the peer range allows. The `engines` field still allows Node.js 18.17 and newer.

**Upgrading:** `npm i github:Demonic1594/ReForgeGiveaways#v2.3.0`. Keep `@tryforge/forge.db` in your own dependencies if you use it.
